sourceInformation.tech: Pixel Engine 0.46.0 (build 2026-11-02), AI Hub session client 1.4.0, esbuild 0.28.2
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine pixel-toon look, original OR sets, primitive busts, canvas tissue
sourceInformation.animation: Engine clock plus sim-driven tool motion, heart pulse, and code-blue needle
sourceInformation.audio: Original chiptune songs, SoundDef effects, and formant gibberish voices. No audio files.
sourceInformation.online: Couch consult on one machine, and AI Hub shared-world for 1 to 4 players. No other network.
sourceInformation.testing: Node sim suite, Playwright on software WebGPU, hub harness on 127.0.0.1. No physical pad, no second person, no iOS Safari, no TV.
sourceInformation.research: The planner read the source Wikipedia page, the hub protocol, and the engine kit, and ran engine spikes. This build followed PLAN.md and the engine docs on this machine.

testingFeedback: Testing caught 13 issues: a string id compared as a number, a magnet pull that snapped, overlapping suture targets, a missing clot flag, a copy-hand that ended before it landed, 2 syringe asserts on the wrong keeper, a title and clock drawn off screen, a vitals readout stuck at 0, finish stats the hub dropped, an idle pad that stole the mouse, a client hand that stayed at spawn, and a dev list that could not jump a stage.

6 would be game-breaking: hooks never left the field, the magnet could not be extracted, Op 5 never closed, the transplant skipped its forced rewind, an idle pad stole the mouse, and a client hand stayed at spawn.
The most helpful test was the skill-1 bot play of every operation, which failed in the live sim and named the stuck entity.
The least helpful test was a screenshot of a menu with no input behind it. Appearance did not show whether focus moved.
engineFeedback: The pure renderSound and Song data made every effect and track testable in Node, and the HUD art-pixel grid matched the fill-mode canvas.
I guessed wrong once: a held entity id is a string, so a numeric comparison never saw the grab. The fixed camera and the audio storage key behaved as the guide describes.
The operation sim, the eight tools, the strains, couch seats, and the shared-world host loop. The engine does not ship a surgery model.
Keeping pad buttons from also pressing keyboard keys, while still reading analog triggers, took the longest to get straight.
A way to mark a gamepad button as "read it yourself" without clearing the whole map by hand.
promptFeedback: The plan named the beats, the tools, and the pass lines, so the game could be built against checks instead of a vibe.
Two documents both said how to boot, and they disagreed about whether screens swap by loading a new game. Pause had to stay inside one game or the music died.
Making one bot clear every operation at the top rank, including the rewind and the two-handed pull, without lowering par.
Ask for the exit-interview counts after the suite has run, and name one file as the only source of the balance numbers.

aiHub.name: The Second Opinion Clinic
aiHub.description: A rainy harbour hospital where telling the truth is the first cut. Keep the patient alive, close the strain, and top the team score.
aiHub.controls: Stick or mouse moves the tool. R2 or click uses it. Right stick or keys 1-8 pick a tool.
